item.title: Bangladesh Missions abroad go offline due to technical issues with DIP server
item.description:
The government is working to address the technical issues as soon as possible and help the Bangladesh Missions abroad deal with visa processing issues, as the server is currently unavailable.
“Efforts are underway to address the technical issues as soon as possible,” a senior official told UNB on Monday night, noting that due to technical issues with the central system of the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP), Bangladesh, the MRV (Machine Readable Visa) server is currently unavailable.
He said all the Missions abroad are facing the same problem. A visa applicant who applied from a European country told UNB that he submitted his visa application online but has been unable to proceed with the process due to the technical issue.
“Although the system indicated that I would receive an email within 24 hours of submitting the application, I have not received any email so far, while repeated calls have gone unanswered,” said the applicant.
Due to the technical issues, the processing of NVR (No Visa Required (NVR)) and visa applications and the issuance of visas at the Bangladesh Missions abroad are experiencing a temporary delay.
The Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP), Bangladesh, is working to resolve the technical issues and restore the central system at the earliest possible time.
The government has requested the applicants to allow additional time for the processing of their applications and to refrain from making repeated enquiries regarding the status of their applications during this period.
Meanwhile, the Embassy of Bangladesh, Berlin, in an urgent notice, regretted any inconvenience caused and appreciated the patience, understanding and cooperation of all concerned.
Applicants will be informed via the websites and Facebook pages of the Missions abroad once the central system is restored and normal visa services resume.
Another official said the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) conveyed to the Missions abroad the information regarding the technical issues last week, as it is applicable to all.
The Embassy of Bangladesh in Bangkok, in a public message on Tuesday, said it informed all visa service seekers that, due to a temporary technical issue with the visa server, applicants may experience difficulties in submitting visa applications and/or receiving visa-related services.
The embassy said the concerned technical team is working to resolve the issue as soon as possible.
Applicants have been requested to bear with the temporary inconvenience and, where possible, avoid making urgent travel arrangements dependent on immediate visa processing until the system is fully restored.
The embassy regretted the inconvenience caused and appreciated the patience and understanding of all concerned.

item.title: Morocco names Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri first woman PM
item.description:
MOROCCO-POLITICS-GOVERNMENT

The king of Morocco on Tuesday named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri the country’s first woman prime minister, the royal cabinet announced, after her party won last week’s parliamentary elections.

Her centre-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) had dominated the vote, winning 97 out of 395 seats in the House of Representatives -- 31 more than the next closest competitor, although the poll was marked by the lowest turnout in two decades.

The royal cabinet said King Mohammed VI has now tasked the 50-year-old, who also served as housing minister, with “forming the new government”.

Speaking shortly after, El Mansouri said in a televised address her appointment was “truly historic”.

“For the first time in our country’s history, a woman is taking on the responsibility of leading the government,” she said. “This is a source of pride not only for me but for all Moroccan women.”

Without an outright majority, the PAM will have to form a coalition with other parties, though the monarch retains broad powers over major policies.

For the new premier, “the work starts today”, she said.

“We will first initiate internal consultations within our party before holding discussions with all political groups.”

El Mansouri joined the PAM in 2008, the year it was founded by current royal adviser Fouad Ali El Himma as a counterweight to the country’s Islamist movement.

She was also the first woman to serve as mayor of Marrakesh, winning the office in 2009 before losing it six years later, then retaking it again in 2021.

‘Restore hope’

El Mansouri’s cabinet will have to tackle several pressing issues including unemployment and living costs, as well as persistent social disparities particularly weighing on young people.

The parliamentary vote came just weeks after tens of thousands of mainly young Moroccan migrants rushed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, a crisis that highlighted socioeconomic frustrations among the youth.

It also came a year after a Gen-Z protest movement took to the streets to demand better health and education.

“We are fully aware that this period will be significant and marked by high expectations from Moroccans, particularly young people,” El Mansouri said. “That is why we will have a programme offering concrete and realistic solutions to citizens’ concerns.”

Her party has pledged average annual economic growth of five percent, inflation of two percent and the creation of at least one million new jobs over its five-year term.

The PAM was followed in the polls by the National Rally of Independents (RNI), which heads the outgoing coalition and won 66 seats.

The right-wing Istiqlal party came third with 65 seats, while the Islamist opposition’s Justice and Development Party (PJD) took 54 seats.

The PJD made significant gains after winning just 13 seats in 2021, having focused its campaign in part on fighting corruption.

Its chief, former prime minister Abdelilah Benkirane, hailed a “victory” but ruled out joining a coalition led by the PAM, which he said was “tainted by fraud”, without providing details.

item.title: Govt regrets repeated attacks, vandalism, land grabs
item.description:
There has already been public unease over the law and order situation. Amid this, a series of incidents involving attacks, vandalism, land grabbing and demolition of buildings have further increased concerns.

In several of these incidents, allegations have been raised against local leaders and activists of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

Referring to the government’s responsibility to ensure citizens’ security, the government has also expressed regret and said it is embarrassed by the incidents.

Information and Broadcasting Adviser to the Prime Minister Zahed Ur Rahman answered questions at a press conference at the Secretariat yesterday, Tuesday, about the attack and vandalism at the Radda health centre in Mirpur and content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio.

Without mentioning the names of the two establishments, he said that if any citizen’s rights are violated, their establishment is demolished or they are attacked, the government is sorry and embarrassed by each incident.

He said, “Because ensuring this security was the responsibility of the government—that is what I mean by embarrassed.”

Regarding action over these incidents, the adviser said that if evidence of anyone else’s involvement is found during the investigation, that person will also be brought under the law. According to him, the impact of these incidents on people is very serious.

It has been learned after speaking to responsible people at various levels of the government and BNP that they are also concerned about the recent incidents.

Amid dissatisfaction over the increase in fuel prices and continuous programmes by opposition parties, these law and order incidents have become an additional concern for the government. In particular, allegations against local leaders and activists of its own party have brought the issue of controlling them to the fore.

Last Thursday night, the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur was demolished and looted allegedly with the intention of grabbing the land. Information has been found about the involvement of several people linked to local BNP politics in the attack on the institution that provides maternal and child healthcare services.

Amid widespread criticism over the incident, the New Guinea Properties housing project in the ECB area was attacked and Salman Muqtadir’s studio there was vandalised at midnight on Saturday.

Early Saturday morning, allegations emerged of an attempt to grab a multistorey building in Shyamoli Housing in Adabor, the capital. On the same day, several hundred people allegedly entered a plot in Mohammadpur’s Chand Udyan, vandalised it and looted money and equipment. In both incidents, allegations have been raised of the involvement of several local leaders and activists of the ruling party.

During a visit to the Radda health centre last Monday, Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman questioned the failure to identify the attackers. He said it was mysterious that the people involved could not be found even after a large number of people had carried out the attack for a long time. He called for action against the criminals without considering their party affiliation.

People concerned said these incidents of land and house grabbing, attacks and vandalism in various parts of the capital have put the government’s image under question. At the same time, the conduct of local leaders and activists of the ruling party and the issue of taking action against them have also come under discussion.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed had already been warning grassroots leaders and activists. At several meetings of the BNP parliamentary party and internal meetings of the party, he warned leaders and activists about criminal activities. He has warned several times, saying, “If you are not careful, no one will be spared.” But questions have arisen over the effectiveness of those warnings in the recent incidents.

Most recently, at a briefing on the law and order situation and contemporary issues at the Secretariat last Sunday, the home minister said that any attempt to deteriorate the law and order situation would be dealt with firmly. Strict measures are being taken against criminals irrespective of party affiliation. He said, “A criminal has no political identity. A criminal is a criminal.”

Meanwhile, National Professor and political analyst Mahbub Ullah has expressed concern and regret over the recent incidents. He told Prothom Alo that over nearly 17 years, BNP’s top leaders to grassroots leaders and activists had faced various forms of persecution, including enforced disappearance, killing and imprisonment.

Even in extremely hostile circumstances, they remained united and fought for better times. That expected better time has come, and the party is now responsible for running the state. Therefore, their responsibility is also enormous. The head of government is also making that effort.

Mahbub Ullah said that, unfortunately, a tendency among leaders and activists to disregard the law appears to have emerged. This is creating a major problem. It is the party’s responsibility to keep these leaders and activists away from criminal activities and restrain them from engaging in such acts.

item.title: Officials: Maitree Express journey time may fall to 6 hours via Padma Bridge
item.description:
The journey time of Maitree Express between Dhaka and Kolkata could be reduced by around three to six hours if the cross-border passenger train is operated through the Padma Bridge-Benapole route instead of the existing Jamuna Bridge-Darsana route, officials said.
The proposed route could also reduce the passenger fare by around Tk1,000, making the train a more convenient alternative to air travel between the two cities, according to sources familiar with the matter.
The Maitree Express, which connects Bangladesh and India, was suspended on July 19, 2024, amid security concerns.
Despite recent political tensions between the two neighbouring countries, the number of Bangladeshi tourists entering India jumped by nearly 80% compared with the corresponding period of the previous year.
According to preliminary data by the Ministry of Tourism, India, over 74,000 people from Bangladesh travelled to India in August.
On September 9, Railways Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam informed Parliament that freight train services are currently operating between Bangladesh and India, while initiatives are being taken to resume passenger train services with the neighbouring country.
Railway Ministry Additional Secretary Ziaul Haque, after the three-day recent inter-governmental railway meeting, told the reporters that no decision has been taken yet on resuming the suspended cross-border train services between Bangladesh and India.
Officials said the two sides are reviewing the possibility of restarting the train services.
The train - Maitree Express - was introduced jointly by Bangladesh and India in April 2008, on the occasion of the Bengali New Year, with the aim of restoring passenger rail connectivity between the two countries that had been disrupted in 1965.
The cross-border service has since served as an important mode of transport for passengers travelling between Bangladesh and India, particularly those travelling for tourism, trade, commerce and medical treatment.
According to Bangladesh Railway sources, a total of 288,360 passengers travelled on Maitree Express from 2022-23 until July 19, 2024. Available records show that around 95% of the passengers were from Bangladesh.
The train maintained an average occupancy rate of 80 to 85%, while the occupancy exceeded 95% during major holidays such as Eid and Durga Puja, reflecting strong demand for the service among Bangladeshi passengers.
Under the existing arrangement for cross-border passenger train operations, Bangladesh Railway receives 75% of the apportioned earnings from passenger bookings on Maitree Express, while the remaining 25% goes to Indian Railways.
Before its suspension, Maitree Express operated through the Tangail-Jamuna Bridge-Ishwardi-Darsana route, covering around 392 kilometres between Dhaka and Kolkata.
According to the approved timetable, the train departed Dhaka Station at 8:15am and was scheduled to reach Kolkata at 4pm, taking seven hours and 45 minutes. On the return journey, it departed Kolkata's Chitpur Terminal Station at 7:10am and was scheduled to arrive in Dhaka at 3:35pm, taking eight hours and 25 minutes.
In practice, however, the journey could take more than nine to 10 hours due to congestion on the railway network, particularly along the Dhaka-Ishwardi-Darsana section.
The opening of the Padma Bridge railway route in December 2024 has created an alternative corridor for trains travelling towards the country's southwestern region and the Benapole border.
The distance and travel time between Kamlapur and Benapole have been significantly reduced through the new route.
While trains previously required more than eight hours for the journey, Ruposhi Bangla Express now covers the route in around three hours and four minutes, according to railway sources.
Railway officials believe Maitree Express could similarly benefit if it is rerouted through Padma Bridge and Benapole instead of the Jamuna Bridge-Darsana corridor.

item.title: বিদেশ ভ্রমণে বিমান টিকিট কেনায় ৩০০ ডলারের সীমা উঠে গেল
item.description:
এখন থেকে বিদেশ ভ্রমণে বিদেশি বিমান সংস্থার যেকোনো দামের টিকিট কাটা যাবে বৈদেশিক মুদ্রায় লেনদেনযোগ্য ডেবিট ও ক্রেডিট কার্ডে। এই সুবিধা কার্যকর হবে বিদেশি মালিকানাধীন ১৭ বিমান সংস্থার ক্ষেত্রে। 

বর্তমানে বৈদেশিক মুদ্রায় লেনদেনযোগ্য ডেবিট ও ক্রেডিট কার্ডে বিমান টিকিট কাটতে ৩০০ ডলারের বেশি খরচ করা যায় না। নতুন নিয়মে, বিদেশি বিমান সংস্থা থেকে বিদেশ ভ্রমণের টিকিট কাটতে খরচের এই সীমা থাকছে না। বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক গতকাল নতুন এক নির্দেশনায় কার্ডে বিমান টিকিট কেনার সুযোগ সহজ করেছে। এর ফলে যেকোনো দামের টিকিট কাটা যাবে দ্বৈত মুদ্রায় লেনদেনযোগ্য কার্ডে। বিমান টিকিট কেনা বাবদ কার্ডে যে অর্থ ব্যয় হবে, তা ভ্রমণ কোটার জন্য সংরক্ষিত বৈদেশিক মুদ্রার সীমার আওতার বাইরে থাকবে। 

এ বিষয়ে নাম প্রকাশ না করার শর্তে বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংকের সংশ্লিষ্ট একজন কর্মকর্তা বলেন, এখন কার্ডে ৩০০ ডলারের বেশি দামের বিমান টিকিট কেনা যায় না। ৩০০ ডলারের বেশি দামের টিকিট কিনতে কার্ড প্রদানকারী ব্যাংকের অনুমতি নিতে হয়। নতুন ব্যবস্থায় বাংলাদেশের সঙ্গে বিমান চলাচল রয়েছে এমন ১৭টি বিদেশি বিমান সংস্থার টিকিট কিনতে টিকিটের পুরো দাম কার্ডে পরিশোধ করা যাবে। তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে এই অর্থ সংশ্লিষ্ট ক্রেতার বিদেশ ভ্রমণ জন্য সংরক্ষিত বৈদেশিক মুদ্রা বা ডলার সীমার সঙ্গে সমন্বয় করা হবে। পরে টিকিটের দাম যখন সংশ্লিষ্ট ব্যাংক বিদেশি বিমান সংস্থাকে পরিশোধ করে দেবে, তখন ভ্রমণকারী বা টিকিটের ক্রেতার কার্ডে ভ্রমণ কোটায় সমপরিমাণ ডলার যুক্ত করা হবে।

item.title: ভোটার তালিকা পরিবর্তন, যে নির্দেশ দিলো নির্বাচন কমিশন
item.description:
ভোটার তালিকায় পরিবর্তন নিয়ে বিতর্কের মধ্যে ভোটার-তালিকা ব্যবস্থাপনার সফটওয়্যার পর্যালোচনার নির্দেশ দিয়েছে ভারতের নির্বাচন কমিশন। শনিবার এ নির্দেশ দেওয়া হয়। ব্রিটিশ বার্তা সংস্থা রয়টার্স এ খবর জানিয়েছে।
একটি সংবাদপত্রের প্রতিবেদনে বলা হয়েছে, ভোটার তালিকা থেকে লাখ লাখ ভোটারের নাম বাদ পড়ার মতো পরিবর্তন নিয়ে প্রধান নির্বাচন কমিশনার জ্ঞানেশ কুমারকে তার দুই সহকর্মী প্রশ্ন করেছিলেন। এর পরই সফটওয়্যার পর্যালোচনার উদ্যোগ নিল কমিশন।
ভারতের বিরোধী দলগুলো অভিযোগ করে আসছে, প্রধানমন্ত্রী নরেন্দ্র মোদির ভারতীয় জনতা পার্টিকে (বিজেপি) সুবিধা দিতে ভোটার তালিকায় কারসাজি করা হয়েছে। তবে নির্বাচন কমিশন বলেছে, প্রতিষ্ঠানের ভেতরে মতপার্থক্য থাকা স্বাভাবিক এবং তাদের সব কার্যক্রম আইন অনুযায়ী হয়েছে।
দ্য ইন্ডিয়ান এক্সপ্রেস চলতি সপ্তাহে এক প্রতিবেদনে জানায়, গত ১০ মাসে দুই নির্বাচন কমিশনার অন্তত ১৪ বার জ্ঞানেশ কুমারের কাছে প্রশ্ন বা উদ্বেগের কথা জানিয়েছেন। এর বেশিরভাগই ছিল গত বছর শুরু হওয়া ভোটার তালিকা হালনাগাদ প্রক্রিয়া নিয়ে।
বিরোধী দলগুলোর পাশাপাশি যুব নেতৃত্বাধীন ককরোচ জনতা পার্টি জ্ঞানেশ কুমারের পদত্যাগ দাবি করেছে। শনিবারের মধ্যে তিনি পদত্যাগ না করলে ২ অক্টোবর দেশজুড়ে বিক্ষোভের ঘোষণা দিয়েছে দলটি।
শনিবার নির্বাচন কমিশন জানায়, একজন জ্যেষ্ঠ নির্বাচন কর্মকর্তার নেতৃত্বে একটি কমিটি সফটওয়্যারটি পর্যালোচনা করবে। কমিটিতে একজন স্বাধীন প্রযুক্তি বিশেষজ্ঞও থাকবেন। সফটওয়্যারটি নির্বাচনসংক্রান্ত আইন ও বিধিমালা মেনে চলছে কিনা, তা যাচাই করবে কমিটি।
এ ছাড়া ভোটার তালিকায় অসঙ্গতি চিহ্নিত হলে সংশ্লিষ্ট ভোটারদের নিয়মিতভাবে সরকারি দপ্তরে হাজির হতে বলার পরিবর্তে স্থানীয় কর্মকর্তারা তাদের বাড়িতে গিয়ে বিষয়টি যাচাই করবেন বলেও জানিয়েছে কমিশন।
